title: The shared control-character filter misses U+061C - the only Unicode Bidi_Control code point it omits - plus the Cf/Zl/Zp invisibles, and the approval card renders them raw beside the argv that will execute
description: Source and a local render confirm a residual gap in the run-3 fix, but not its security outcome. web._shown (web.py:33-37) sends every template output through display.escape_controls with keep_newlines=True (web.py:94), and that class does neutralise the run-3 payloads: rendering the real _approvals.html through web.py's exact Jinja wiring turns U+200E/U+200F/U+202A-E/U+2066-9 into literal \uXXXX escapes while markupsafe escapes markup. The class is hand-written (display.py:13,15) and covers 11 of the 12 Unicode Bidi_Control characters: U+061C ARABIC LETTER MARK is absent, and so are U+200B-200D, U+2060, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+2028 and U+2029. Measured in the approved sandbox, all of them survive raw in both the command <pre> and the affected-path cell of the same card, and cli._safe (cli.py:33-35) is byte-identical, so the terminal approval view carries the same gap rather than disagreeing with the web view. What is not established is whether any of them lets the card read as a different command in the operator's browser. U+061C is bidi class AL, a strong right-to-left character, not an isolate: on its own it cannot reverse a run of ASCII letters (they stay strong L), and its bidi effect is limited to the resolved direction of adjacent neutral punctuation sitting between two of them. U+2028/U+2029 are mandatory line breaks that would split one argv into two visual lines inside the same pre block without hiding either line, and the remaining characters are invisible rather than reordering. That leaves a display-integrity question whose answer lives in the renderer, which no surface in this audit can observe.
claimed_root_cause: display.py:13 and display.py:15 enumerate the control and bidi characters by hand. The set is C0/C1 plus exactly Bidi_Control minus U+061C, so ALM (Bidi_Control=Yes, bidi class AL) together with the Cf invisibles U+200B-200D, U+2060, U+FEFF, U+00AD and the separators U+2028/U+2029 pass through. web._shown applies that class to every str template output (web.py:35-36, 94) and cli._safe applies it to the terminal view (cli.py:35), so both human surfaces share the residual gap; nothing else filters those characters on the path from the stored approval args to the card.

trace.description: The lowest-trust agent principal posts an exec call whose args.command it chooses; policy.decide routes a non-allowlisted program to approval, and nothing normalises or rejects unusual code points in the string.

The approval is created with the agent's original args dict and the system preview (service.py:318; preview adds no affected paths for a plain echo/python3 command). approvals.py:56 persists the args with json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False), so the code points are stored as bytes the card will show and service.py:398/421 later executes.

Pending approvals, including the original args and the system-computed preview paths, are listed and rendered into _approvals.html by the same view that serves both GET /ui/approvals and the approve/deny POST handlers.

finalize runs _shown over every output expression, which applies escape_controls(value, keep_newlines=True) to str values only (web.py:33-37); no template uses |safe or Markup, so this hand-written class is the entire filter for the card.

trace.scope: exec command <pre> (and the affected-path cell at line 14)
trace.description: The command is emitted into <pre> without short(), so only autoescape plus display.py:13/15 apply. Locally rendered with U+061C, U+200B-200D, U+2060, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+2028 and U+2029 placed in the command and in an affected path, every one of them reaches the HTML raw in both cells while U+200E/U+200F/U+202A-E/U+2066-9 come out as visible \uXXXX escapes.

evidence.description: UNSAFE is [\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f\u200e\u200f\u202a-\u202e\u2066-\u2069]. Tested in the sandbox against the 12 code points with Bidi_Control=Yes: it matches 11 of them and does not match U+061C; it also does not match U+200B-200D, U+2060, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+2028 or U+2029.
_UNSAFE_KEEP_NEWLINES, the variant the web UI actually uses, repeats the same class minus tab/newline, so the U+061C and Cf/Zl/Zp omissions are identical on the web path.

_shown returns non-str values unchanged and calls escape_controls(value, keep_newlines=True) for str; a direct escape_controls call leaves U+061C, U+200B, U+200D, U+2060, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+2028 and U+2029 unchanged in both keep_newlines modes while escaping U+200E/U+200F/U+202A-E/U+2066-9.

tpl.env.finalize = _shown is the only string filter registered for the web templates (filters['short'] is added at line 93), so the card's command and path cells depend entirely on the display.py class plus markupsafe autoescape.

The exec command is emitted into <pre> with no short() and no filter; in the local render the markup payload was escaped ('<script>') and the run-3 bidi set became literal escapes, while U+061C/U+200B/U+2028 stayed raw.

Container-derived affected paths are rendered by the same finalize; the local render shows the same nine code points raw inside the path cell, so the second human-facing string on the card is equally unfiltered.

cli._safe is escape_controls(str(s), keep_newlines=False); measured on the same command its output is byte-identical to web._shown, so the terminal approver shares the omission and there is no web-only asymmetry left to exploit.

exec runs str(args.get('command','')) from the approval row loaded at service.py:398 and executed at service.py:421, so the argv keeps the exact code points the card displayed; only the display side is filtered.

Calibration: the run-3 remediation text for the shared class already listed 'Optionally add U+061C to _UNSAFE', so the ALM omission was known and deliberately left optional; this record is that follow-through, not a re-opened run-3 isolate spoof.

blockers: No browser or terminal renderer is reachable from the approved sandbox (python3 plus the repo and jinja2/fastapi only, no network, no display), so the rendered order of the residual code points cannot be observed. The local run proves the reachability half only: U+061C, U+200B-200D, U+2060, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+2028 and U+2029 arrive raw in the card's <pre> and path cell while the argv executed by service.decide (service.py:398,421 -> service.py:126) keeps the same code points.

The decisive fact is whether a residual code point makes the card read as a different command. U+061C is bidi class AL, a strong right-to-left character that cannot reverse ASCII letter runs; U+2028/U+2029 add a mandatory break inside the same pre block but hide nothing; U+200B-200D/U+2060/U+FEFF/U+00AD are invisible and only affect how individual characters join. Which of these, if any, yields a misstatement depends on the browser engine, the resolved base direction and the font stack, none of which the repository pins (base.html:23 sets white-space: pre-wrap and no unicode-bidi isolation).

Which browser engine versions, fonts and terminal emulator the operator actually uses is unknown to this audit, and that choice decides whether ALM and the separator characters produce any visible difference between the approved view and the executed command.

Next, still offline with dummy data: render the same fragment from a loopback static file in a local browser engine (Playwright Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) and capture the rendered line/baseline order of the pre block for payloads built only from the residual set - (a) echo 'x' + ALM + ';>' + ALM + ' ; python3 /workspace/job.py', (b) the same command with U+2028 placed before the trailing echo, (c) a ZWSP inside one option token - then compare each capture with the argv string and record whether the card states a different command. Regression, worth doing regardless of the browser result: add U+061C to both regexes in display.py plus the Cf/Zl/Zp invisibles (keeping tab/newline in the keep_newlines variant) and add a test asserting escape_controls neutralises U+061C, U+200B and U+2028 in both modes; grep shows no test currently exercises this class.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-side and non-destructive: on a dummy sandbox, queue one pending exec approval whose command contains two ALMs around a ';' and a U+2028 between two shell commands, open /ui/approvals in the operator's real browser and the same request in the terminal 'agentbox approve' view, and compare what is rendered with the exact argv returned by GET /approvals/{aid} (or the audit 'tool_execute' args). No probing of live endpoints beyond the owner's own instance.

title: Unauthenticated failed POST /login writes one permanent hash-chained audit row per attempt, with no rate limit, aggregation or retention
description: web.py:130-140 serves POST /login with no principal and no cookie requirement. On a token mismatch it calls box.log_human("ui_login_failed", None, {}) at 136; service.py:590-594 forwards that to audit.append, which takes the single process-wide audit lock, runs BEGIN IMMEDIATE, reads the previous chain hash, inserts a row and commits (audit.py:162-185). Nothing rate-limits, deduplicates, aggregates, caps or prunes these rows: api.py:113 registers _NoFraming as the only middleware, deploy/Caddyfile:4-6 reverse-proxies /login with no rate or body limit, and audit.py contains no DELETE, VACUUM or retention code. Removal is not merely unimplemented but blocked: the audit_no_delete trigger (audit.py:37-38) rejects DELETE and verify() rejects any id gap (audit.py:233-234), so pruning rows later breaks the integrity check the operator relies on. The only precondition is same_origin (web.py:132), which returns True when the Origin header is absent (api.py:131-133), so a plain HTTP client reaches the write. Locally reproduced at the ASGI layer with the real AuditLog/AgentBox/handler: one wrong-token POST added exactly 1 ui_login_failed row, 250 such POSTs added 250 durable rows at ~11.5 ms each, and 6 concurrent clients sustained ~270 rows/s while raising the latency of an ordinary agent tool_request append from ~4.6-5.5 ms to ~36-40 ms. The same handler has the inverse defect: a non-ASCII token makes secrets.compare_digest raise TypeError at web.py:134, so the request returns a bare 500 with 0 rows recorded and the client also chooses which attempts enter the chain.
root_cause: An unauthenticated, attacker-paced durable write into the append-only security record: the failed-login path uses the same serialized hash-chained append that gates tool executions, with no per-source or global rate limit, no aggregation, and no retention or compaction for the rows it creates - and the append-only triggers plus verify()'s contiguity check leave no legitimate way to remove them afterwards.
intended_behavior: Anonymous authentication failures should be rate-limited and aggregated before they reach the audit chain (for example one "N failures since T" summary per source per interval), so one unauthenticated client cannot unilaterally grow the operator's security record or monopolize the audit lock every other append and read needs; the audit store should have a documented retention/compaction scheme that keeps chain verifiability (signed checkpoints plus archived segments). A malformed credential should be compared as bytes (or rejected on an ASCII check) so it becomes a recorded 401/400 instead of an unrecorded 500.

trace.description: def login(request: Request, token: str = Form(...)) has no principal, session or cookie requirement; the only precondition is the same_origin call at 132, and same_origin (api.py:131-133) returns True when the Origin header is absent.

A wrong token falls through the compare_digest at 134 to box.log_human("ui_login_failed", None, {}) and then renders the error page at 139; a non-ASCII token raises TypeError at 134 before this line and returns 500 with nothing recorded.

log_human forwards the event to self.audit.append(actor="human", event=event, sandbox_id=sid, payload=payload) at 592; an AuditWriteError would become a 503, but on success the row is durable in SQLite.

trace.scope: INSERT INTO audit under the process-wide lock
trace.description: append() takes self._lock at 162, BEGIN IMMEDIATE at 163, reads the last hash at 165, inserts the row at 179-184 and commits at 185; every other audit append (including tool_request/tool_result) and every human read or verify() waits on the same lock.

evidence.description: One process-wide threading.Lock (self._lock) serializes all appends, so unauthenticated login failures share one queue with tool-call records.

The database runs in WAL mode; nothing bounds rows, pages or file size, and agentbox/audit.py contains no DELETE, VACUUM, retention or compaction path (grep: 0 hits for DELETE FROM audit, VACUUM, retention).

The audit_no_delete trigger (37-38) aborts every DELETE, so the rows an anonymous client creates cannot be removed at all, and verify() at 233-234 rejects any gap in ids, so trimming the table breaks the integrity check.
The failed-login path is gated only by same_origin; api.py:131-133 returns True when the Origin header is absent, so a direct HTTP client with no cookie or Origin reaches the audit write.
_NoFraming is the only middleware added (app.add_middleware(_NoFraming)); there is no rate limiter, body cap or connection throttle anywhere in the FastAPI app.
The shipped proxy is a bare reverse_proxy agentbox:8765 with no rate_limit and no request_body directive, so the deployment adds no bound in front of /login.

The audit database lives at AGENTBOX_HOME/agentbox.db, and deploy/docker-compose.yml:28 bind-mounts ${AGENTBOX_HOME_DIR} from the host, so growth consumes operator-owned disk that outlives the container.

The human audit page calls box.audit.verify() (and api.py:273 exposes it as GET /audit/verify), which loads the entire audit table under the same lock, so attacker-added rows directly lengthen the operator's integrity check.

conditions.description: None - a wrong form token and no cookie; no Origin header required.
The control plane is reachable through the shipped Caddy proxy, and AGENTBOX_HOME/agentbox.db persists across restarts with no pruning path.
The audit table is append-only at the database level (audit_no_update/audit_no_delete triggers) and verify() requires contiguous ids, so rows written by an anonymous client are permanent.
The serialized append bounds the rate (~86 rows/s from one client, ~270 rows/s with 6 concurrent clients) but never the total number of rows.

execution.attacker_perspective: An unauthenticated client posts the login form with a wrong token as fast as the server answers, adding one durable audit row and one acquisition of the global audit lock per request, for as long as it likes.
payloads:
POST /login HTTP/1.1
Host: agentbox.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 10

token=nope
POST /login ... token=%C3%BCn%C3%AFcode   (compare_digest raises TypeError -> 500, 0 rows recorded)
instructions: In the approved sandbox, set AGENTBOX_HOME to a scratch directory and instantiate the real AuditLog(settings.db_path), Policy.load, ApprovalStore, DesktopControl and AgentBox from the audited tree; register the real web.register handler on a FastAPI app with the same_origin predicate copied verbatim from api.py:131-133. The only stand-in is box.sandboxes (web.register reads box.sandboxes.runtime at registration time), because api.build() calls docker.from_env() at sandbox.py:162 and the sandbox has no Docker socket.

Drive POST /login through fastapi.testclient.TestClient with urlencoded bodies, no cookie and no Origin header, and count rows with event='ui_login_failed' in AGENTBOX_HOME/agentbox.db before and after each request.

Repeat with a non-ASCII token (token=%C3%BCn%C3%AFcode) and compare status code and row count; then hammer the handler from 6 threads while timing ordinary audit.append calls of the shape the tool path uses and audit.list() reads.
execution.observed_result: Independent reproduction matched and extended the candidate: 1 wrong-token POST added exactly 1 ui_login_failed row; 250 further wrong-token POSTs added 250 rows at ~11.5 ms per request (~86/s) with no rejection, cap or 429 at any point; 6 concurrent clients reached ~270 rows/s. Latency of a normal agent tool_request audit.append rose from a 4.6-5.5 ms baseline to 36-40 ms while the login flood ran, because both take audit.py's single lock. A non-ASCII token returned 500 (TypeError: comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported) and added 0 rows, so the same client can also keep its attempts out of the chain.

remediation.strategy: Rate-limit and aggregate failed logins before the audit append: a per-client-address token bucket plus a global cap, recording a compacted 'N failures since T' summary per window instead of one row per attempt (never dropping the fact that failures happened). Give the audit store a retention scheme that preserves chain verifiability (signed checkpoints plus archived segments) so operator disk growth is bounded and auditable. Compare credentials as bytes, or reject non-ASCII input explicitly, so a malformed credential is a recorded 400/401 rather than an unrecorded 500, and keep the 'audit before action' rule intact for tool paths.

likelihood.reason: A form POST with a wrong token from any client that can reach /login; no cookie, Origin header or token knowledge required, and the Caddy deployment in front of it has no rate limit.

impact.reason: Permanent, unbounded growth of the append-only audit database on operator-owned host disk with no legitimate deletion path, plus measurable contention on the single audit lock that every tool-call append and every human verify() needs (4.6-5.5 ms baseline to 36-40 ms under a 6-client flood). Per-row cost is small (~200-250 bytes and ~11.5 ms serialized), so the effect is slow disk growth and degraded audit latency rather than immediate outage.

confidence.reason: Every trace and evidence line was re-checked in the 9805d91 tree, and both the durable one-row-per-attempt growth and the non-ASCII unrecorded 500 were reproduced locally against the real handler, service and audit code with only the Docker-backed SandboxManager stubbed.
